name: hunt and dodge packs
why: hunt orcs and other monsters the warrior can beat, back off to heal in time, and leave before a gargoyle or bone knight pack catches it mid-fight

hunt.says: Fight the nearest creature the warrior can beat (orcs and similar) and finish it before looking for more; loot valuables when nothing is fighting.

transitions.when: A group is coming at the warrior that together is too strong for it: two or more creatures each about as strong as the warrior or stronger (gargoyles, bone knights), or any creature much stronger than the warrior, while it is fighting or hurt.
transitions.unless: Only weak creatures like orcs are coming, or the strong ones are far off and not heading toward the warrior.

transitions.when: Health is below about half, or is falling faster than bandages bring it back.

regroup.says: Step back from the fight and let bandages and potions work; only hit what is right on the warrior.

transitions.when: Health is back above three quarters, or nothing is attacking any more.
Health keeps dropping while backing off, or more creatures are joining, or a strong creature (gargoyle, bone knight) is coming.

out.says: Leave: run until nothing hostile is in sight, ignoring loot; spellcasters will keep hitting from range, so keep running instead of stopping to fight.

transitions.when: Nothing hostile is in sight or close any more.

recover.says: Stay away from the pack, rest and bandage up until health is high before hunting again.

transitions.when: Health is nearly full and no strong creature or pack is in sight.
A pack or a strong creature is coming at the warrior again.
